_note: Original advanced concept questions for binary search.

questions.title: Sorted requirement
questions.code:
nums = [2, 4, 6, 9, 12]
target = 9

Can mid tell us which half to remove?
questions.prompt: What must be true for ordinary binary search on a list?
choices: The list has exactly two values
questions.explanation: Binary search uses order to discard half the list. Without reliable order, that discard is unsafe.

questions.title: Middle index
questions.explanation: The range has indexes 0 through 6, so the middle index is 3.

questions.title: Move right
questions.prompt: In an ascending sorted list, `nums[mid]` is less than the target. What should happen next?
questions.explanation: If the middle value is too small, the target can only be to the right.

questions.title: Move left
questions.prompt: In an ascending sorted list, `nums[mid]` is greater than the target. What should happen next?
questions.explanation: If the middle value is too large, the target can only be to the left.

questions.title: One item left
questions.code:
low = 3
high = 3

One index is still left to check.
questions.prompt: Why does a closed-range binary search use `low <= high`?
choices: The one remaining index still needs to be checked.
questions.explanation: When low equals high, there is still one possible item left.

questions.title: Stuck bounds
questions.code:
low = 0
high = 1
mid = 0

Buggy update:
low = mid
questions.prompt: Why can `low = mid` cause an infinite loop?
questions.explanation: If mid equals low, setting low to mid keeps the same range.

questions.title: Binary search steps
questions.prompt: Arrange the main binary search loop steps.
lines: Set low to the first index and high to the last index.
While low is less than or equal to high, compute mid.
If the middle value is the target, return mid.
If the middle value is too small, move low right.
questions.explanation: Each loop checks the middle, then removes the half that cannot contain the target.

questions.title: Beyond arrays
questions.code:
Answer range:
1 2 3 4 5 6
F F F T T T

Find the first True.
questions.prompt: Binary search can also work on an answer range when what property is true?
questions.explanation: A monotonic condition changes in one direction, so the search can discard half the range.
